title: You Are Invited to Max's Party
text:
Dear Friends,
You are invited to Max's seventh birthday party! It will be on Saturday at {number} o'clock in our backyard. Please wear something {adjective}, like a party hat or a pair of {plural noun}.

First we will play Pin the Tail on the {animal}. Then everyone will get a turn to {verb} in the bounce house. Max's dad will be {verb ending in ing} by the grill all afternoon, so come hungry!

For lunch we will have pizza, apple slices, and a giant bowl of {plural noun}. The cake is shaped like a {noun} and has {color} frosting. After cake, Grandpa will play music, and we will all dance {adverb}.

Please do not bring a present that is too {adjective}. Max already has lots of toys. Just bring a big smile and a {adjective} {noun}!
Love,
Max's Mom

title: Thank You, Aunt Rosa
text:
Dear Aunt Rosa,
Thank you for the birthday present! When I opened the box, I found a {adjective} {noun} inside. I have always wanted one. Mom says it is the most {adjective} gift I have ever gotten.

I use it every day, and I keep it under my {noun} at night. On Monday, I showed it to my teacher, Mrs. Green. She {past tense verb} so hard that she had to sit down. On Tuesday, my little brother tried to {verb} with it. Now it smells a little bit like {food}.

Thank you also for the card with {number} dollars in it. I am saving it to buy a pet {animal}, a box of crayons, and two {plural noun}.

Please come to my next party. We will eat cake, wear {adjective} hats, and dance {adverb} in the kitchen. Please bring your {plural noun}!
Love,
Sofia

title: Grandma's Famous Birthday Cake
text:
This is how my grandma makes my birthday cake every year. You will need a big bowl, a wooden spoon, and a {adjective} grown-up.

First, mix two cups of flour with three {plural noun}. Stir it {adverb} until it looks {adjective}. Next, crack two eggs and add a spoonful of {food}. That is the secret part, so do not tell anyone.

Pour everything into a pan shaped like a {noun}. Bake it for {number} minutes. While you wait, you can {verb} around the kitchen and sing to the oven. Grandma says the cake likes songs about {plural noun}.

When the cake is cool, cover it with {adjective} frosting and put a tiny {noun} on top. Add the candles and turn off the lights. Everyone will start {verb ending in ing}. Grandpa always takes the first bite and says, "This tastes like {plural noun}!"

title: Rules for the Bounce House
text:
Welcome to the bounce house! Please read these rules before you go in. Uncle Ted wrote them on a big piece of {color} paper.

Rule one: Take off your shoes and your {plural noun}. Put them in the basket next to the {animal}. Rule two: Only {number} kids can be inside at one time. If there are too many, the bounce house gets {adjective} and starts to wobble.

Rule three: No food inside. Last year my cousin brought in a {noun}, and we are still finding little pieces. Rule four: Please do not {verb} on the walls. Bouncing is fine. Jumping is fine. But {verb ending in ing} is not allowed, ever.

Rule five: If you feel {adjective}, come out and sit with Grandpa. He will give you a cup of water and a {adjective} {noun}. Have fun, bounce {adverb}, and say thank you to the {plural noun} on your way out!

title: The Day I Turned Seven
text:
Dear Diary,
Today I turned seven! I woke up early because my dog, Biscuit, was {verb ending in ing} on my bed. Mom made pancakes shaped like {plural noun} with a side of {food}. They were a little bit {adjective}, but I ate them all.

At school, my class sang the birthday song to me. My best friend Leo sang so {adverb} that the class fish hid behind a {noun}. Then I got to wear the birthday crown. It is made of paper and {plural noun}.

After school, Grandpa came over with a present. It was a {adjective} {noun} with a big bow on top! I {past tense verb} around the living room {number} times.

Now I am in bed, and I am very tired. Being seven is {adjective}. Tomorrow I am going to {verb} all day long.

title: The Party Game Awards
text:
Here are the winners of today's party games. Every player did a {adjective} job.

The Musical Chairs prize goes to Ava. She sat down so {adverb} that the chair squeaked. She wins a shiny {noun}. The Egg and Spoon Race was won by Jamal. He kept his egg on the spoon, even when a {animal} ran in front of him. He wins {number} stickers and a bag of {plural noun}.

The Hula Hoop Contest ended in a tie. Mia and Ben kept {verb ending in ing} for ten whole minutes. Each of them gets a {adjective} medal and a cup of {plural noun}.

Finally, the prize for Best Dancer goes to Grandpa Joe. He {past tense verb} across the patio and shook his {body part} like a {adjective} noodle. Next year, he says he will {verb} even better.

title: How to Blow Out Your Candles
text:
Blowing out birthday candles is a very important job. First, wait until everyone has finished singing. Do not start early, or Aunt May will sing again, and she sings very {adverb}.

Next, close your eyes and make a {adjective} wish. You can wish for anything, like a pet {animal} or a house made of {plural noun}. Keep your wish a secret!

Then take a deep breath. Fill your cheeks with air until they look like two {adjective} {plural noun}. Lean over the cake, but do not put your {body part} in the frosting or bump the {noun} on top.

Now blow! If all the candles go out, everyone will clap and shout, "{exclamation}!" If one candle stays lit, just try to {verb} a little harder. Then the birthday kid gets the first piece, and the dog gets a {noun}. Eat your cake {adverb} with a {adjective} fork!

title: Breaking News from the Backyard
text:
Good afternoon. This is Lily Park with breaking news from Oak Street, where a birthday party is happening right now. At one o'clock, the guests arrived carrying presents and {plural noun}. The birthday girl, Rosie, {past tense verb} at the front door and gave everyone a {adjective} hug.

At two o'clock, there was trouble. The wind blew the balloons into a {adjective} tree. A tall neighbor got them down using only a ladder and a {noun}. The crowd cheered {adverb}.

At three o'clock, the piñata was finally opened. Out came candy, toys, and {number} tiny {plural noun}. Kids were seen {verb ending in ing} all over the grass. One {animal} was seen wearing a party hat.

Right now, Rosie's dad is asking everyone to {verb} before the ice cream melts. Today's flavor is {food}. Experts say it is the most {adjective} party of the year. Back to you in the studio, {name}!

title: What Is in Your Party Bag
text:
Thank you for coming to Nora's birthday party! Here is what is inside your party bag.

One bouncy ball. Please do not bounce it inside, or your grown-up might get {adjective}. Two stickers shaped like {plural noun}. Put them on your notebook or your {noun}. Three pieces of candy. Nora says the {color} ones taste like {food}.

One tiny jar of bubbles. Dip the wand and blow {adverb}. If you blow too hard, you will just {verb} instead. One {adjective} pencil with a {noun} on the end.

One paper crown. Wear it at dinner and tell everyone you are the king or queen of {place}. One small surprise at the very bottom. Nora says it might be {verb ending in ing} when you open the bag.

Thank you for being such a {adjective} guest. See you next year, and please bring your {plural noun}!

title: Dad's Party Checklist
text:
Dad made a checklist for my birthday party. He wrote it with a {color} marker and hung it on the fridge with a magnet shaped like a {noun}.

First, he will blow up {number} balloons and tie them to the mailbox. Then he will hang a sign that says Happy Birthday in {adjective} letters. Mom says last year's sign was a little too {adjective}.

Next, he will set up the snack table. It will have juice boxes, cheese crackers, and a tall stack of {plural noun}. He will also practice {verb ending in ing} so he can be the party clown. His clown nose is made of {food}.

At four o'clock, he will carry out the cake and sing {adverb}. Then he will {verb} with the kids in the yard and hand out {adjective} prizes. Last of all, he will sit on the couch, take off his {plural noun}, and {verb} for the rest of the day.
